top_signal.title: My childhood friends and I started a business together, but one friend's father is treating us like employees. I'm considering walking away. Am I overreacting?
top_signal.summary: I'm looking for honest, unbiased advice because I'm dealing with a situation that's affecting both my business and a childhood friendship.   A while ago, two childhood friends and I decided to start a small IT business together. Two of us handle the technical side, including developing websites, software, and other digital solutions. Our third friend isn't from a technical background and also has a separate job, so his day-to-day contribution to the technical work is different from ours.   Initially, I was genuinely excited. Building something of our own with friends we've known for years sounded like a great opportunity.   However, things have gradually started going in a direction I never expected.    The main issue is our third friend's father.    He's become heavily involved in our business discussions. Whenever we meet him, he asks about our clients, our progress, and whether we've updated his son about everything.   At first, I thought he was simply trying to help us grow. He often speaks positively about us and gives us motivational advice. But over time, I've started feeling that there's an underlying expectation that his son should be the face of the business while the other two of us handle all the technical work behind the scenes.   He's explicitly said things along the lines of, "Let him handle the clients, and you guys work in the backend."
